ruleset.name: Amazon Listing Content Guidelines
ruleset.note: This is the only ruleset loaded. No external retailer documentation is used. Every recommendation cites these IDs. Rules are data, not code: a different retailer or an updated policy loads as a new file without touching the engine.

tiers.T1: Objectively checkable from the text. Deterministic code, no model.
tiers.T2: Needs reading comprehension or quality judgment. LLM, with the rule supplied as context.
tiers.T3: Real gap, but not fixable from the fields we hold. Surfaced, never auto-edited.

rules.name: Length
rules.text: Keep titles under 200 characters including spaces. Shorter, scannable titles (~80-150 characters) generally perform better on mobile.

rules.name: Structure
rules.text: Recommended pattern: Brand + Model/Key Feature + Product Type + Size/Count/Color (if applicable).

check.criterion: Does the title follow Brand + Key Feature + Product Type + Size/Count/Colour, with the most important information first?

rules.name: Capitalization
rules.text: Capitalize the first letter of each word (title case). Do not write in ALL CAPS.

rules.name: No promotional or subjective claims
rules.text: Do not include phrases like "Best", "#1", "Cheap", "Sale", "Free Shipping", "100% Guaranteed", or excessive punctuation (e.g. "!!!").

rules.name: No keyword stuffing
rules.text: Do not repeat the same keyword multiple times or cram unrelated search terms into the title.

rules.name: Required identifiers
rules.text: Include size, count, color, or flavor when the product has variants, so customers can distinguish this SKU from others.

check.criterion: Does the title name the specific variant (size, count, colour or flavour) so a shopper can tell this SKU from its siblings?

rules.name: Count
rules.text: Use up to 5 bullet points.

rules.name: Length
rules.text: Keep each bullet under roughly 200-255 characters; lead with the most important information first.

rules.name: Format
rules.text: Start each bullet with a short capitalized header phrase (e.g. "DURABLE DESIGN:") followed by a benefit-oriented sentence. Avoid ending with a period if using a fragment style, but be consistent.

rules.name: Benefits, not just features
rules.text: Explain what the feature means for the customer (e.g. not just "rubber material" but "durable rubber construction stands up to aggressive chewing").

check.criterion: Does each bullet explain what the feature means for the shopper, rather than only naming the feature?

rules.name: No pricing, promotions or shipping claims
rules.text: Do not mention price, discounts, deals, or shipping/guarantee terms in bullets - these belong in seller-controlled merchandising, not content.

rules.name: No ALL CAPS sentences
rules.text: Emphasis words may be capitalized (e.g. a short header), but full bullets should not be written in all caps.

rules.name: No unverifiable superlative or medical claims
rules.text: Avoid "best", "cures", "guaranteed", "clinically proven" (unless substantiated with certification), or claims about health/safety benefits that cannot be verified.

rules.name: Length
rules.text: Up to approximately 2,000 characters. Use complete sentences and short paragraphs (avoid a single wall of text).

rules.name: Content
rules.text: Expand on bullet points with use-case context, materials, care instructions, sizing guidance, and any relevant compliance/safety notes (e.g. "always supervise pets during use").

check.criterion: Does the description add use-case context, materials, care or sizing guidance and any safety note, beyond repeating the bullets?

rules.name: No contact info, external links or promotional pricing
rules.text: Do not include phone numbers, email addresses, URLs to external websites, or pricing/promotional language ("buy now," "limited time," "free shipping").

rules.name: No HTML
rules.text: Do not paste raw HTML tags into the description field.

rules.name: Consistent tone
rules.text: Avoid first-person seller voice ("we are proud to bring you...") - write in an informative, third-person, customer-facing tone.

rules.name: Minimum count
rules.text: Provide a minimum of 1 main image; best practice is 5-7 images including main + lifestyle + infographic + size/scale reference.

rules.name: Main image requirements
rules.text: Pure white (RGB 255,255,255) background, product fills ~85% of frame, no text/logos/watermarks/props on the main image.

check.reason: Needs the image pixels. The CSV holds URLs only, so this is reported, never auto-fixed.

rules.name: Resolution
rules.text: At least 1000px on the longest side to enable zoom functionality.

check.reason: Needs the image pixels. Reported as a gap for the creative team.

rules.name: No pricing or promotional claims
rules.text: No pricing or promotional claims anywhere in title, bullets, or description ("sale," "best price," "cheap," "discount," "free gift").

rules.name: No time-sensitive claims
rules.text: No time-sensitive claims ("order now," "while supplies last," "limited time offer").

rules.name: No guarantees or warranties language
rules.text: No guarantees/warranties language unless it reflects an actual registered Amazon program (e.g. do not self-declare "100% money-back guarantee").

rules.name: No unverifiable superlatives
rules.text: No unverifiable superlatives ("#1 best-selling," "best in the world") without substantiation.

rules.name: No reviews or testimonials in content
rules.text: No reviews/testimonials referenced in content ("5-star rated by customers," "customers love it").

rules.name: No competitor mentions
rules.text: No competitor mentions (brand names of other sellers/products) in title, bullets, or description.

check.criterion: Does the copy name another seller's brand?

rules.name: No seller contact info or external links
rules.text: No seller/company contact information or external links.

rules.name: Backend search terms
rules.text: Backend search terms should complement (not repeat) the front-end title/bullets, stay under the platform's character limit, and avoid duplicate or irrelevant terms. Not directly assessed by this skill.

check.reason: The supplied data has no backend keyword field, and the ruleset itself marks this as out of scope for the skill.
